flags.evidence: Opened page/index.html from disk (file://) in Chromium at 1440x900 (dsf 1) and 390x844 (dsf 3); no page errors. The brief asks the page to talk to both kitchens and makers, and the hero's first screen at 1440 pairs one action per side: filled 'Publish your kitchen's hours' (x780,y316, https://ovenhour.example/kitchens, brief-supplied) and outlined 'Tell us the shift you need' (x780,y389, href #makers) with the note 'Your note goes to the founders' inbox with your county on it'. So the maker action is the second primary action of a two-sided page; it repeats in the end band ('.band-end .btn-line', href #makers). At both widths, clicking it scrolls to form#makers ('Tell us the shift you need'). I filled 'Mecklenburg, NC' and 'sourdough' and clicked 'Send the founders your shift'. The status read 'Opening your mail app with this note. If nothing opens, copy it to makers@ovenhour.example: ...' and the browser requested mailto:makers@ovenhour.example?subject=Shift%20wanted%20in%20Mecklenburg%2C%20NC&body=... (script.js line 119; the form's action attribute on index.html line 248 is the same address). The brief supplies only ovenhour.example/kitchens and no maker channel or email address, so this primary action ends at an invented email address. That case is listed under 'Counts'. The up-front note ('It opens as an email to the founders; nothing is stored here') does not fall under the 'local action' exemption, because the action does not stay local: it addresses mail to an invented inbox, not a destination the brief supplied.
